extraFacts.fact: A hose or tube size code is in sixteenths of an inch: 02 is 1/8 inch, 03 is 3/16 inch, 04 is 1/4 inch, 05 is 5/16 inch, 06 is 3/8 inch, 08 is 1/2 inch, 10 is 5/8 inch, 12 is 3/4 inch, 14 is 7/8 inch and 16 is 1 inch.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 / SAE J1131 dash-size convention used across brass fitting makers

extraFacts.fact: Brass tube fittings, couplings and hose barbs are normally classified under HS subheading 7412.20 (copper-alloy tube or pipe fittings); the importer's customs broker has the final say.

ISO 7-1 covers pipe threads where the pressure-tight joint is made on the thread, such as the BSP taper (R) thread; ISO 228-1 covers pipe threads where the joint is not made on the thread, such as the BSP parallel (G) thread; ASME B1.20.1 is the general-purpose NPT pipe thread standard; ASME B1.20.3 covers Dryseal pipe threads, including NPTF; SAE J512 covers automotive tube fittings including flareless compression.
extraFacts.source: ISO 7-1, ISO 228-1, ASME B1.20.1, ASME B1.20.3, SAE J512

extraFacts.fact: SAE J2494 covers push-to-connect fittings for air brake tubing and FMVSS 571.106 covers brake hoses and their end fittings; the maker of the DOT push-in fittings states compliance with both. SAE J844 covers nonmetallic air brake tubing. DOT-approved air brake fittings are for compressed-air brake systems.
extraFacts.source: SAE J2494, SAE J844, FMVSS 571.106 (as stated on the listing)

faqs.q: What is the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow used for?
faqs.a: The Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow is a 90° hose mender in brass for low-pressure hose secured with a clamp on air, water, fuel and coolant lines. The listing has 4 part numbers.

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers on the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow?
faqs.a: Each part number is the base number IH-BR-177 plus size codes. IH-BR-177-04-04 is 1/4" hose barb, and IH-BR-177-08-08 is 1/2" hose barb. The Sizes tab gives the size on every end; quote the part number in full when you order.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow come in?
faqs.a: The Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow has 4 part numbers. For example IH-BR-177-04-04, IH-BR-177-06-06, IH-BR-177-08-08 (1/4" hose barb to 1/2" hose barb).

faqs.q: How do I pick the right size of the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow?
faqs.a: Match the hose to the barb and the thread to the port: the hose inside diameter sets the barb size, and the other end must match the thread on the port. For example IH-BR-177-06-06 is 3/8" hose barb. Check the thread form before ordering; our [guide on what to send for a fittings quote](/blog/what-to-send-for-a-fittings-quote) lists what helps.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature is the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow rated for?
faqs.a: The manufacturer publishes no pressure rating for this hose end, and an assembly is rated to the lower of the hose and the end connection. Tell us the hose and working pressure for the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow and we confirm the fitting.

faqs.q: What is the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow made of?
faqs.a: The body is brass. Brass suits air, water and fuel lines but not strong acids or ammonia. Ask us if you need another metal for the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow.

faqs.q: Does the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow follow a standard?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard for the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow, only its material, form and sizes. If your project needs a specific standard or a material certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can document for IH-BR-177-06-06.

faqs.q: What does the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow connect to?
faqs.a: The Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow connects to low-pressure hose pushed over the barb and secured with a clamp. Matching parts are on our [brass hose barbs](/c/brass-hose-barbs) shelf.

faqs.q: How should the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow be installed?
faqs.a: Push the hose fully onto the barb of the Brass Hose Barb Mender, 90° Elbow and secure it with a hose clamp over the barb; do not rely on the barb alone. Seal tapered pipe ends with sealant or tape; see our [guide to hose barbs and push-lock fittings](/blog/hose-barbs-and-push-lock-fittings).

faqs.q: What is the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter used for?

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-BR-172-06-06 on the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter?
faqs.a: The base number IH-BR-172 is followed by one code per end, each a size in sixteenths of an inch. Here 06 is 3/8" NPSM, 06 is 3/8" NPTF. The same rule holds on every row of this listing, so IH-BR-172-02-02 is 1/8" NPSM (1/8-27) x 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27).

faqs.q: How do I pick the right size of the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter?
faqs.a: Match the hose to the barb and the thread to the port: the hose inside diameter sets the barb size, and the other end must match the thread on the port. For example IH-BR-172-06-06 is 3/8" NPSM (3/8-18) x 3/8" NPTF (3/8-18). Check the thread form before ordering; our [guide on what to send for a fittings quote](/blog/what-to-send-for-a-fittings-quote) lists what helps.

faqs.q: What does the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter connect to?

On its other end it takes a female NPT or NPTF port, such as a valve, tank or manifold port. Matching parts are on our [brass NPTF pipe fittings](/c/brass-nptf-pipe-fittings) shelf.

faqs.q: How should the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter be installed?
faqs.a: Push the hose fully onto the barb of the Brass NPSM Male × NPTF Male Ball-Seat Adapter and secure it with a hose clamp over the barb; do not rely on the barb alone.
